newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission close to deal on new work hours law.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission close to deal on new work hours law.

text.p: Senior European Commission officials were close to agreeing on Thursday how to apply European Union rules on working hours and rest times to workers not now protected by the provisions.
"There are no more fundamental problems," a Commission official told Reuters.
He was speaking after a meeting to prepare a Commission discussion paper on ways to extend the EU's Working Time Directive, which limits the average work week to 48 hours.

The legislation, which was unsuccessfully challenged in court last year by Britain's former Conservative government, currently excludes nine million EU workers, including truck drivers, trainee doctors and offshore workers.

A consensus was emerging around the idea of applying the directive to "non-mobile" workers in the excluded sectors while letting individual sectors set specific rules for their "mobile" workers, officials said.
Non-mobile workers would be guaranteed a maximum 48-hour week, night shifts of an average of eight hours, four weeks paid leave a year and at least one day off a week.
The offshore oil industry, where the work patterns do not follow a normal working week, would be excluded entirely from the draft directives.

The discussion paper, prepared by the services of Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn, was originally scheduled for adoption on Wednesday, but is now expected to be rubber-stamped by commissioners on July 16.
But before then, the text will have to be clarified and the distinction between non-mobile and mobile workers made more explicit, one official said.
"I think what we expect to see... is a much more effective and logical (proposal)," he said.
